change: second round: out-of-fold stage-2 scores replace stage-1 scores as neighbour inputs

change: final stage 2 refitted with confident test rows as pseudo-labels (p >= 0.9, <= 0.01, capped)

lesson: pseudo-labelling test rows does not help on the leaderboard

change: both stages use the sharper 127-leaf lightgbm (best_params) instead of the smoother one
hypothesis: checks that the stacking gain holds on a different base model before relying on it for the final picks
lesson: stacking on the sharper parent scores below E19, but +0.0032 over its own unstacked parent E01, so stacking helps on both bases and the smoother base is better

change: 5 seeds at every stage (stage-1 scores, round-2 scores, final model), averaged
hypothesis: seed averaging is the most reliable small gain for boosted trees and removes seed luck (research: about +0.0002 to +0.0005)
lesson: seed bagging moves the public score by less than noise (spearman 0.992 with E22); kept as the low-variance anchor candidate for the final picks

change: add mean/max of neighbours out-of-fold logistic regression scores, logits clipped to the training range
hypothesis: a linear model makes different mistakes from trees, so its neighbour scores add signal; main value is a different candidate for the second pick
lesson: best public score so far but within noise of E25; 16.6% of test logistic regression logits hit the clipping bounds, a sign of drift; structurally different, so a candidate second final pick

change: rank blend of E25 (weight 2) with E24 (weight 1)
hypothesis: research puts 2:1 as the most weight the sharper stack deserves; tests whether its different errors help
lesson: the 2:1 blend with the sharper stack neither helps nor hurts

change: graph features and neighbour scores for training rebuilt under the test rule: unlabelled training rows count towards degree but contribute no features or scores
hypothesis: 47% of training neighbours are unlabelled rows with features while 49% of test neighbours are featureless edge-only nodes linked only to test steps; 25% of test rows vs 0% of training rows have no visible neighbour, so every neighbour feature is built differently in train and test
lesson: matching training neighbourhoods to the test rule does not move the public score, as the test-like proxy predicted; the mismatch is real but the models barely rely on the affected features

change: rank blend of E28 (weight 3) with a 5-seed lecture-04 MLP on matched features plus neighbour scores (weight 1)
hypothesis: a different learner family adds diversity; research: cross-family blends beat the best single model
lesson: best public score so far (+0.0015 over E26); just under the 0.003 bar against its parent, but the first time a different learner family added to the stack, matching the research that cross-family blends beat the best single model

change: neighbour mean/max over all 159 kept features instead of the top 30 (single seed in stacking stages)
hypothesis: 16 of the 30 most informative neighbour features fall outside the day-1 top 30
lesson: neighbour aggregates over all features add nothing over the top 30

change: stack in the 3:1 blend is the unmatched E26 instead of the matched E28
hypothesis: tests whether the MLP gain carries over to the best unmatched stack; spearman 0.989 with E29, a real hedge
lesson: new best public file; +0.0020 over its own stack E26, so the MLP gain carries over to the unmatched stack; matched vs unmatched stack remains noise

change: the 5-seed MLP alone, no stack
hypothesis: its public score sets the right blend weight (Bates-Granger: about 2:1 if near 0.95, 3:1 or less if near 0.93); never a final pick
lesson: MLP alone 0.9454 vs stack 0.9589: weight curve stack 0.9589, 3:1 0.9615, 1:1 0.9599, MLP 0.9454; Bates-Granger with errors 0.041 and 0.055 gives the best MLP weight 0.36 at zero error correlation and 0.23 at 0.5, and the observed curve fits a correlation near 0.5, so about 3:1 is the right weight

change: MLP trained on every stack input of the matched graph instead of the reduced linear feature set
hypothesis: a stronger second family may lift the blend; risk that it becomes too similar to the trees
lesson: full-feature MLP reached 0.9916 alone but the blend is 0.9992 correlated with E29, a wasted slot

change: equal weight on the matched stack and the MLP instead of 3:1
hypothesis: with E32 (MLP alone) maps how the score moves with the MLP weight; spearman 0.980 with E29
lesson: equal weight is past the optimum; keep the MLP near a quarter of the blend

change: pagerank, reverse pagerank, clustering, k-core, component size and in/out balance added to the stack
hypothesis: structural features are complete in both periods, unlike neighbour feature averages
lesson: univariate auc up to 0.632 (component size, inverted) but on the forward-chaining proxy +0.0003 for the smoother model and -0.0006 for the stacked model, worst-step auc -0.011; the stack already captures structure through neighbour scores

change: the MLP in the best blend averaged over 15 seeds instead of 5
hypothesis: less seed luck in the quarter of the blend that comes from the MLP; protects the private score, public change likely noise
lesson: identical to E31 within rounding, as its 0.9999 correlation predicted; kept as the steadier final-pick version of E31

change: add a second MLP trained on own features only (no graph inputs) as a third family: stack 6, graph MLP 2, own MLP 1
hypothesis: a learner that never sees the graph makes different mistakes again
lesson: own-feature MLP: validation 0.9810, spearman 0.874 with the graph MLP and 0.726 with the stack; the 6:2:1 blend is 0.9974 correlated with E31, and heavier weights exceed the Bates-Granger estimate (0 to 0.1), so the weight is set by a diagnostic upload first

change: the own-feature MLP alone
hypothesis: its public score sets its blend weight: about 0.945 -> build 3:1:1, about 0.93 -> weight too small to test, below 0.91 -> close the family
lesson: own-feature MLP alone 0.9231, between the 0.91 and 0.93 bands of the decision rule; error 0.077 against 0.038 for E31 puts its best blend weight near 0 to 0.05, too small to show on the leaderboard, so the own-MLP family is closed

change: direction-aware features: senders out-degree, receivers in-degree, reciprocal payments, two-hop reach, chain count, source and sink shares
hypothesis: research (round 10): fan-in/fan-out patterns help boosted trees on transaction graphs
valid_auc: proxy fwd auc 0.9778 vs 0.9784, ap 0.9227 vs 0.9232
lesson: weak on their own (best univariate 0.400) and slightly negative in the stack

change: smooth each score towards the mean score of its neighbours, weights 0.1-0.5, 1-3 rounds
hypothesis: research (round 10): the smooth step of Correct and Smooth propagates graph signal without labels
lesson: gets steadily worse with more neighbour weight; the stack already uses neighbour scores

change: MLP in the 3:1 blend replaced by a stronger MLP: quantile-scaled inputs, periodic numeric embeddings, weight averaging over the last 5 epochs
hypothesis: research (round 10): a stronger but still different MLP lifts the blend; accept if valid auc >= 0.9918 and spearman with the stack <= 0.80
lesson: public 0.96209 vs 0.96206 for E31: the much stronger MLP (validation 0.9974 vs 0.9918) changes nothing on the leaderboard, consistent with its higher correlation with the stack (0.878) cancelling its extra strength

change: the stronger MLP alone
hypothesis: its public score sets its blend weight; if close to the stack (0.960), heavier weights such as 2:1 or 1:1 come next
lesson: the stronger MLP alone scores 0.9598, almost level with the stack E26 (0.9601) and far above the old MLP (0.9454); with near-equal errors the two-forecast formula puts its best weight near one half, so heavier blends (1:1) come next

change: stack 2 : old MLP 1 : stronger MLP 1
hypothesis: keeps the old MLP for its different mistakes and adds the stronger one; spearman 0.991 with E31
lesson: best public score so far and rank 7th; within the 0.003 band against E31 but consistent with the diagnostic that the stronger MLP deserves more weight

change: personalised PageRank per time step seeded on out-of-fold scores: exposure, exposure minus own restart share, neighbours mean/max exposure (lecture 08 collective inference)
hypothesis: GOTCHA: neighbours mean exposure was a top fraud feature
lesson: neighbour scores already carry what PageRank propagation adds

change: Louvain communities per time step: size, mean/max score of other members, share above the 90th percentile (lecture 08 p.60)
hypothesis: community influence beats individual connections (lecture claim)
lesson: communities add nothing over one-hop neighbour scores here

change: stack gets one-hop score spread and two-hop score aggregates (max, mean, q75, high-score counts) built from round-2 out-of-fold scores; blended 2:1:1 with both MLPs as E43
hypothesis: Oskarsdottir et al.: first- and second-order score features rank near the top for fraud
lesson: two-step score features improved every offline number (both views) and validation, but the public score fell 0.0014 within noise; second-order score features add no measurable gain over one-hop stacking here

change: reconstruction error from quantile scaling + 10-component PCA fitted on all rows without labels: overall, top-30 and rest errors, senders and receivers mean error (lecture 04)
hypothesis: label-free anomaly signal, strong alone
lesson: univariate about 0.85 inverted but drifts (train-vs-test 0.64) and the stack already captures it

change: decoded feat_4/feat_5 as input/output counts: spent share, observed-input share, unspent outputs, unobserved inputs, 1-in-1-out flag
hypothesis: UTXO mechanics from the competition overview; trees cannot form ratios
lesson: raw counts are already in the model; ratios add nothing

change: the adversarially trained MLP alone (FGSM eps 0.03, lecture 07)
hypothesis: its public score sets its blend weight
lesson: best single model so far, above the stack (0.9601) and the stronger MLP (0.9598); with an error below the stack the two-forecast formula gives it at least half the weight

change: stack : old MLP : stronger MLP : adversarial MLP at 1:1:1:1
